theory: The procedure must handle the real domain before testing rationality: an even-index root of a negative number is not real, while a root of zero is rational. Because the definition permits rational radicands, 'perfect nth power' must explicitly include powers of rational numbers: $\sqrt{4/25}=2/5$ is not a surd, so an integer-perfect-power test is insufficient. Likewise, the square-root criterion used in practice.development[5] must be restricted to whole-number radicands or stated in terms of rational squares.
